# AGENTS.md — AI Session Protocol for YITC v2

This file is a **SOURCE** the primary AI agent's startup seed is assembled from — read at every session start AND after every `/compact` — a Worker via its assembled VIEW (`graph/worker-seed.md` **and every continuation part it chains to**); the Controller reads the SOURCE parts directly in the read-order (each single-read-safe — SPEC-0007 §5c). It defines what the AI does, in what order, with what discipline.

## At session start (BEFORE any tool call)

**Handbook SOURCE manifest** — the generation order the views assemble from (your runtime read is
your audience's assembled VIEW, NOT these files one-by-one — §Per-audience read-order below; read the
per-file source directly only when authoring/regenerating the handbook):

<!--GEN:read-order:numbered GENERATED from HANDBOOK_READ_ORDER in bin/yitc-v2 — DO NOT EDIT; regen via `bin/yitc-v2 graph build` (SPEC-0007 §5b)-->
1. **CHARTER.md** — the 8 principles + non-goals. Anti-complexity (principle #1) governs every subsequent decision.
2. **AGENTS-SESSIONS.md** — session types + write-flow + scope boundary — part 2 of the AGENTS protocol (a separate startup-served file, read it after AGENTS.md).
3. **AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md** — worker protocol, gates, filing, planning & references — part 3 of the AGENTS protocol (a separate startup-served file, read it after AGENTS-SESSIONS.md).
4. **LIFECYCLE.md** — the 9-stage task lifecycle. You'll work through one of these stages per session turn.
5. **QUEUE.md** — where tasks live (active / done / parking-lot). Source of truth for «what to do next».
6. **GRAPH.md** — how specs link to code. Use before designing anything new (Principle 1 filter (1) «existing analog?»).
<!--/GEN:read-order-->

The files in this read-order — the generated `HANDBOOK_READ_ORDER` set — ARE the handbook (<vendor-adapter>.md is a vendor adapter pointing here, NOT counted in the canonical handbook cap per CHARTER §Principle 2). The AGENTS protocol is SPLIT across **AGENTS.md + AGENTS-SESSIONS.md + AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md** for single-Read safety (SPEC-0120); a Worker receives all parts inside its assembled view, the Controller reads them directly as source parts of the read-order (§Per-audience read-order below). Held within the CHARTER §Principle 2 size budget, which counts the FULL generated set incl every split part (the authoritative home — the cap number is not restated here, so it cannot diverge). Read the WHOLE of your audience's seed.

**Per-audience read-order (SPEC-0007 §5c + SPEC-0127).** The read-order above IS the interactive Controller's runtime read — it reads the SOURCE parts DIRECTLY, in that order (its audience union = ALL sections = these files, each single-read-safe; no assembled monolith — SPEC-0007 §5c; the generated `graph/controller-supplement.md` stays a derived reference view, not a runtime read). A **dispatched Worker** (`--type build`) reads the SMALLER slice: its whole startup handbook is the generated `core`+`worker` seed, also **IN PLACE OF** the full files above. **That seed is a CHAIN of size-bounded parts, not one file :** read **`graph/worker-seed.md`** and then **every continuation part it names** (`graph/worker-seed-2.md` …) — part 1 lists the whole chain, and each part points at its next hop. The chain exists because a GENERATED startup read surface is held to the same one-bounded-read ceiling as a source doc (SPEC-0007 §5c / SPEC-0120 §3): the pre-split single file ran ~1275 lines / ~51K tokens and the reader physically truncated it. **One part is NOT the seed** — stopping early silently starves you of rules. A Worker never dispatches, runs the queue picker, or authors/stages plans, so the `controller`-only sections (orchestrate/dispatch governance, the picker, the plan-lifecycle FSM, the controller startup echoes, the owner-facing register rules) are NOT in its bootstrap (the fail-safe default is over-inclusion — a section leaves the worker seed ONLY via an explicit `<!--AUDIENCE:controller-->` tag, never by omission — SPEC-0127 §2). This routing is delivered on BOTH load surfaces: the manual read-order (here — this note is itself `core`, so a Worker sees it inside part 1 of its seed) AND the vendor auto-inject (the engine `<vendor-adapter>.md` names the same chain, so a Worker's `worktree new`+`cd` re-floors exactly `core`+`worker`).

**Kernel-prefixed retrieval under `-C` (SPEC-0092).** Every handbook retrieved-tier pointer
(`graph query SPEC-XXXX`) names a KERNEL spec by its bare id. In a `-C <consumer>` session that owns its
OWN spec at the SAME id, a bare `graph query SPEC-XXXX` resolves the CONSUMER's spec (consumer-own wins) — so to fetch the kernel contract the pointer names, re-issue it with **`--kernel`**:
`bin/yitc-v2 graph query --kernel SPEC-XXXX` (forces the engine/kernel spec + body). In the engine's own session `--kernel` is a no-op (own IS the kernel). Bare lookup is unchanged —
defaulting it to kernel would break a consumer reading its OWN specs, so the flag is the reader's explicit
escape on a collision, not a handbook-wide rewrite.

**Also auto-read `MEMORY.md`** (repo root — the project-local governed buffer, SPEC-0039 — split out of SPEC-0007 §6). **Worker exemption (SPEC-0039 §0):** a dispatched
WORKER (`session start --type build`, SPEC-0039 audience `background`) does **NOT** auto-read this
buffer — its startup read-set is the mandatory handbook seed + the active stage bundle only. The
buffer's cross-session-continuity content is controller-oriented (continuation seeds / near-term
to-dos) — irrelevant to a task-bounded worker AND a confabulation source. The rest of this
paragraph governs the Controller / interactive (auto) session that DOES auto-read it. It is
**non-authoritative** — NEVER cited for
closure/governance/`from:`, holds no unique durable state (truth = corpus + journal); the handbook +
specs WIN on any conflict (P7). Every entry is **short, read-by-all, consume-once, deleted after
use** — anything that must PERSIST routes by purpose to its durable home (SPEC-0091), it is not a
MEMORY entry. TWO entry kinds: an unmarked **short to-do-NOW line** (the default — a near-term note
any session may consume; not audience-filtered) and explicitly-marked **bounded temporary
instructions** (`[instruction] [audience: …] [until: …]`) a session MAY act on — only ever a POINTER
to a governed provisional (a plan-in-trial / an in-flight task / an explicit expiry), NEVER a
free-standing rule. At startup apply the **READ-ONLY self-filter**: ignore entries whose audience is
not you or whose lifetime has passed; an UNMARKED note is a plain to-do-NOW line, NOT an instruction
(fail-closed — it cannot grant a standing-action mandate). **Even a MARKED mandate/continuation seed
does NOT itself authorize starting work: plan/task continuation begins only on a LIVE owner cue in the
current session (SPEC-0039 §4) — never self-select a seed thread at startup.** The session that CONSUMES an entry
DELETES it as a governed WRITE at that moment (its worktree / artifact closure) — never a startup
write, never deferred; the weekly sweep is only a stale-leftover backstop. Full rule: `bin/yitc-v2
graph query SPEC-0039` (the buffer is NOT handbook — it does not count against the §Principle-2 cap).

**MANDATORY — scan `bin/yitc-v2 --help`** (`task` / `audit` / `graph --help` for subcommands) — the CLI is the only exhaustive, current list of available verbs; the handbook prose names them by use, but the surface grows per shipped task. This scan is **required, not advisory**: `--help` emits a session fetch-receipt and the session-entry work-verbs (`worktree new` / `task file` / `land`, whichever fires first) REFUSE until this session has scanned it (`_require_help_read`) — the enforcement backstop for the class-#17 adoption gap that a pure-advice line could not close. Scan it immediately AFTER `bin/yitc-v2 session start` **carrying your session ref** — `YITC_SESSION_REF=<the ref `session start` printed> bin/yitc-v2 --help` (a `-C` consumer: `YITC_SESSION_REF=<ref> <engine>/bin/yitc-v2 -C <repo> --help`) — because the fetch-receipt is SESSION-TIED: it is credited ONLY inside a window anchored by THIS session's own `session_started`, so a scan run WITHOUT the carry lands under a different ref, is not credited, and the first gated verb refuses (so its fetch-receipt post-dates the `session_started` anchor `_require_help_read` windows from — a pre-anchor Phase-1 scan is NOT credited either), NOT only after `/compact` (symmetric with §After-/compact — that rescan is likewise post-anchor, since a `/compact` emits no new `session_started`) — to avoid the adoption gap (CHARTER §AI failure classes #17). The verb-gate cannot reach advice given BEFORE any verb runs — that gap is closed HERE by this mandatory wording.

**`--help` is the verb INVENTORY; the canonical write-flow lives in `§Writes happen in a worktree`** — the ONE home for the worktree-isolated path every mutating action follows. `session start` surfaces a navigational POINTER to that home as the `binding:[seed]` general-verb seed line (SPEC-0007 §5a seed class / SPEC-0051), so the intent→home routing is delivered at startup without duplicating the sequence (Single-SoT — SPEC-0005 rule 8: this is a navigational pointer, not a restated rule).

**[REF_AVAILABLE]** Need a consolidated report (rules, verb governance, …)? Run **`bin/yitc-v2 graph query --type view`** to discover the saved query-lenses FIRST, instead of re-assembling one bespoke under load ( — discovery rests on a deterministic catalog, not AI memory).

**Deviation capture — HOLD ALL SESSION.** The moment something is not as it should be — a manual fallback because no verb covered the case, a redundant re-read, a duplicate tool call, an artifact contradiction — emit `deviation_captured` **immediately**: `bin/yitc-v2 event deviation_captured --data '{"relates_to":…,"impact":…,"fingerprint":…}'` (`kind` is OPTIONAL at capture — decided in triage — normative home SPEC-0056 §1; established by §2). **No worktree needed** — run the `event` append from anywhere, INCLUDING the main checkout; the line is folded into main by the next `land` ( — see §Writes-happen-in-a-worktree EXCEPTION). Capture is a **reflex, not a judgement** — do NOT pre-decide "is it worth it" (that judgement is exactly what kept frictions invisible). **Invert it: the felt "not worth capturing" hesitation IS itself the trigger — emit first, let triage decide value later.** And if the owner (or any external prompt) had to surface a deviation you'd already noticed and silently passed on, the reflex already MISSED — capture it now AND mark `captured_via: owner-surfaced` so the miss stays countable (class **E-0044**). ONE event, no RCA in the moment; most stay event-only and never become a case file. Silently working around a deviation makes the recurrence invisible and it costs again. (`friction_captured` is the retired legacy name — read-only.) Full procedure (aspect-audits, promotion, case files): `patterns/error-friction-tracking.md`. **Pre-claim premise-false corollary (SPEC-0133):** when the deviation you just captured is a **dispatched worker's** discovery — at pre-claim, BEFORE `worktree new` — that the ready task's PREMISE is false (unmet precondition / out-of-scope / self-unsatisfiable), the capture is NOT the exit. Its **covering verb** is `bin/yitc-v2 task refuse T-XXXX --reason <why>` (the pre-claim refusal, verb-execution discipline above) — run it so fleet-verdict reads `refused(pre-claim)` / needs-decision, never `launch-stall` («never came up — re-dispatch»). A bare capture-then-exit is the MISS that loops the re-dispatch (2/2 on 2026-07-10).

**Verb-execution discipline — MANDATORY, HOLD ALL SESSION.** Where a CLI verb **covers** an action — it is the governed path that produces that action's required journal + artifact side-effects — that verb is the **only obligatory path**; doing its work **by hand is FORBIDDEN**. Hand-work skips the verb's deterministic journal emit, so the governed action is **invisible across sessions** — work the journal never saw did not, for the system, happen (the failure / closed). The verb inventory is `bin/yitc-v2 --help` / the graph, **never enumerated here** (the surface grows; enumerating it here would drift). **Narrow exceptions:** (a) **emergency mode** — the tooling itself is broken (`patterns/emergency-mode.md`); (b) a **genuine gap** — no verb covers the case. This is the operational expression of Principle 2 (no substantive action without durable capture) + Principle 5 (one journal).

**Journal is a capability you know and use.** Beyond the graph, the journal
(`events.jsonl`) is a queryable record of **intent + action + reads** across sessions. Reach
for it ON DEMAND — like `graph query` — for orientation, prior-art («did we already discuss /
decide this?»), cross-session state, and recovery. Query via **`bin/yitc-v2 journal query`** — the
segment-aware reader (SPEC-0190 rule 4); a raw text search of the journal PATH reads the LIVE segment only and
silently answers «not found» for older history. See §Journal — know it + query on demand. NOT mandated per action.

**V2 self-contained protocol.** This repo-local handbook (CHARTER + the AGENTS protocol
(AGENTS.md + AGENTS-SESSIONS.md + AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md) + LIFECYCLE + QUEUE + GRAPH) is **authoritative** for AI session behaviour when cd-ed into
`<repo-root>/`. Global server surfaces — `<host-home>/<vendor-adapter>.md`,
`<host-home>/MEMORY.md`, `<host-home>/<provider-config>/commands/`, `<host-home>/yitc-workspace/`,
`<host-home>/registry.yaml`, `<host-home>/bin/` — are **non-normative read-only provenance**
unless explicitly cited by a V2 artifact (decision YAML / task YAML / spec / handbook section).

`~/<provider-config>/commands/yitc.md` = thin 2-step pointer (cd + Read project-local).
See full isolation contract + cross-territory cleanup list.

**Session log awareness.** The primary AI tool writes a
durable, per-session transcript artifact to a provider-specific local path (typically
`~/<tool-config-dir>/.../<session-uuid>.{jsonl,json}` — exact location varies by tool).
It records every owner message, AI response, and tool call with timestamps, append-only,
persisting across `/compact`. This artifact = **transient input for parser/adapter**
, NOT durable citation target. For chat-derived rationales (Principle 2) cite

Materialization happens via parser/adapter sync.

**Bare session-log pointer permitted ONLY for routine low-stakes forensic reference**,
NOT load-bearing governance. For load-bearing citations cite the materialized journal
entry (verbatim excerpts captured there as a side-effect of materialization). Recovery
verb: `bin/yitc-v2 journal sync --session-ref <id>` for orphan-tail forensic cases.

### Journal — know it + query on demand (recovery is one use)

The journal (`events.jsonl`) is a first-class capability, **peer to the graph** — a queryable
record of **intent + action + reads** across sessions. Reach for it ON DEMAND (not per action) for:

- **Orientation** — what was recently directed / done / discussed (incl. by parallel sessions).
- **Prior-art / anti-reinvention (#5)** — «did we already discuss or decide this?» — catches
  discussions that never became an artifact.
- **Cross-session coordination** — the shared truth of concurrent work; no single transcript has it.
- **Intent-vs-actual** — `owner_directive` (intent) vs `commit_landed` / `task_closed` (action);.
- **Recovery** — finding a lost artifact/discussion (the search order below).

Query via **`bin/yitc-v2 journal query`** (parity with `graph query`) — `--type` / `--task` /
`--session` / `--grep` / `--since` / `--limit`. It is the **segment-aware** reader: the journal is ONE
logical history across bounded physical segments (SPEC-0190 rule 1), so a raw text search of the journal PATH
sees the live segment alone and reports an older row as absent.

**Recovery search order** — «Not in `tasks/`/`decisions/`/`plans/`» ≠ «doesn't exist». Before
concluding absence, sweep in THIS order (most decisive first):

1. **Owner-directive journal FIRST** — `bin/yitc-v2 journal query --type owner_directive` (the
   `.yitc/` hook-tail's `owner_input`, which is out of the segment contract — SPEC-0190 rule 1b — and
   is still grepped directly). It records the request's **original wording verbatim**, so query it in
   the **language the owner used** (`--grep <phrase>`) — an artifact may be authored in a different
   language than the ask.
2. **The journal** by `--type` / `--task`; **`git log --all -S<term> --grep`** (commits + `from:` trailers).
3. **Artifact bodies** (`plans/` `decisions/` `ideas/`) — search by BOTH the question's words
   **and** likely solution words. Filenames encode the **solution** framing, not the question, so
   title-match misses.
4. **Provider transcripts** + `.yitc/discussion-drafts-pending/raw-*.md` — LAST. Cross-session work
   lives in the shared **journal**, not in any single session's transcript.

The awareness-ledger (`.yitc/awareness-ledger-current-session.yaml`) holds **read-receipts only** —
which atoms were loaded — NOT discussion content; useless for «what did we discuss».

**Verification:** before your first SUBSTANTIVE action — any edit/write, or any mutating/governed command (the read-only startup calls a session's own `session start` needs are exempt) — voice BOTH anchors aloud in your response — (1) the **anti-complexity** principle (CHARTER §Principle 1), (2) the **deviation-capture reflex** (capture the moment something is not as it should be — / above; full procedure `patterns/error-friction-tracking.md`). One principle is not enough — both must be held from the start. If you cannot voice both, re-read.

## After `/compact`

Re-read your audience's **whole seed** (a Worker: the assembled `graph/worker-seed.md` + EVERY continuation part it chains to; the Controller: the SOURCE parts directly, in the read-order — SPEC-0007 §5c), EXACTLY as at **§At session start** — assembled from the SOURCE manifest **<!--GEN:read-order:arrow generated from HANDBOOK_READ_ORDER — DO NOT EDIT; regen via `graph build`-->CHARTER.md → AGENTS.md → AGENTS-SESSIONS.md → AGENTS-PROTOCOL.md → LIFECYCLE.md → QUEUE.md → GRAPH.md<!--/GEN:read-order-->** (the floor trigger-map `graph/floor-trigger-map.md`), in the §At-session-start canonical order — then **re-run the WHOLE §At-session-start startup read identically** (including its `-C <consumer>` engine-path resolution: re-read the seed by *re-reading*, never by re-running `bin/yitc-v2 session start` — EXCEPT the single sanctioned seed-receipt refresh, see §Refresh the seed_read receipt below). A `/compact` is a context-eviction event — it may evict ANY mandatory-tier file — so restore the WHOLE seed, NEVER a subset (SPEC-0007 §5). One list, re-loaded identically at start and after compact — the coherence invariant (SPEC-0007 §5b). **Then the genuine compact-specific deltas below — these are NOT in the re-readable seed (they are `session start` echoes or compact-only actions), so re-reading the seed does NOT restore them; act on each explicitly:**

**Per-audience re-delivery (SPEC-0007 §5c + SPEC-0127).** "Restore the WHOLE seed" is scoped to the reader's OWN audience — a `/compact` restores the WHOLE of YOUR audience's seed, never a sub-subset of it (the §5b coherence invariant re-stated per-audience, NOT weakened). A **dispatched Worker** (`--type build`) re-reads its whole `core`+`worker` seed — the generated **`graph/worker-seed.md` AND every continuation part it chains to** (IN PLACE OF the full files above); re-reading part 1 alone is exactly the "sub-subset" this invariant forbids. The vendor auto-inject (`<vendor-adapter>.md` names the same chain) re-floors the same set on the post-compact cwd re-load, so both surfaces restore identically. The interactive **Controller** re-reads its whole `core`+`worker`+`controller` seed — the SOURCE parts directly, in the read-order (the same files it read at session start; each single-read-safe — SPEC-0007 §5c). Each audience's seed is ONE map realized twice (session start + post-`/compact`); the two MUST stay identical PER AUDIENCE — a Worker is never starved of a rule it needs, a Controller still restores everything.

**Co-design MUST (pointer — SPEC-0007 §5b).** This re-read list is the post-`/compact` home for ALL startup-delivered content, not just the handbook files. So any change that adds/changes what `session start` delivers (a file, the `binding:[seed]` seed how-to, the type-dispatch, an echo line) must co-design its post-`/compact` re-delivery in the SAME change — per the §5b coherence invariant. Full rule body lives single-SoT in SPEC-0007 §5b (`bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0007`); not restated here.

**Continuation-seed survival (pointer — SPEC-0007 §5b option (a)).** The continuation-seed discipline (produce one fresh-session hand-off at a clean seam — interactive sessions only — fired on EITHER of two triggers now: the OWNER's "refresh session" cue, OR a data-driven telemetry threshold (`bin/yitc-v2 session context` reaching the configured % of the window); still NOT AI self-estimation of context) is a `binding:[seed]` rule whose body lives in **SPEC-0114**, not in re-read handbook prose; its session-start seed line is evicted by a `/compact`. Re-deliver it here: in an interactive session, after this re-read, hold SPEC-0114's rule — fetch `bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0114`. (Pointer only — the rule is not restated here, P5.)

**Context-bounded autonomous-continuation re-delivery (pointer — SPEC-0007 §5b).** The context-bounded autonomous-continuation doctrine (within an owner-authorized plan-drive/batch the Controller proceeds across seams without an inter-seam owner cue, stopping only on a genuine owner decision or the `session context` threshold; plus the non-blocking-batch rule) is a `binding:[seed]` rule whose body lives in **SPEC-0126**; its session-start general-verb seed line is a `session start` echo evicted by a `/compact` (re-reading the handbook seed does NOT restore it). Re-deliver it here: in an interactive session, after this re-read, hold SPEC-0126's rule — fetch `bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0126`. (Pointer only — the rule is not restated here, P5.)

**Also rescan `bin/yitc-v2 --help`** (or `bin/yitc-v2 task --help` / `audit --help` / `graph --help`) — CLI surface grows per shipped tasks; post-compact AI must know the current subcommand set to avoid the adoption gap (per CHARTER §AI failure classes #17). (Post-anchor by construction — a `/compact` emits no new `session_started`, so the original session's anchor still credits this rescan at the read-gate; the "scan AFTER `session start`" ordering the initial-start §At-session-start MANDATORY paragraph fixes must not be re-broken here.)

**Refresh the seed_read receipt (per SPEC-0007 §5b / SPEC-0050 §8).** The audience-seed read-gate's receipt is EPOCH-scoped: a `/compact` advances the context epoch, so your pre-compact receipt is now STALE and every governed/mutating verb will refuse `seed_read_stale_epoch` until you refresh it. Its sole producer is `session start`, so — AFTER the full-seed re-read above — **re-run `bin/yitc-v2 session start` ONCE** to re-stamp the receipt for the new epoch. This is the ONE sanctioned post-`/compact` re-run of `session start` (a NARROW exception to "re-read the seed by re-reading, never re-run `session start`" at the top of this section): that rule governs restoring seed CONTENT (done by re-reading the FILES above); this refreshes the RECEIPT only. Safe by construction — the read-gate window is EARLIEST-anchored, so the extra `session_started` does not move your window origin. (The refusal message self-delivers this if you forget.) **Scope:** this ONE re-run is SOLELY for the seed receipt — it is NOT how you restore the `cross`/`debt`/kernel-signaling/MCP echoes below; those still require their explicit re-fold/re-fetch verb (do NOT rely on this re-run to surface them — each names its own verb).

**Stage-bundle freshness (per SPEC-0007 §5a).** The full-seed re-read above stays unconditional. ADDITIONALLY, lifecycle-scoped content is delivered on the stage-entry axis (`stage <NAME>`) and a `/compact` evicts it from context — so **when a session has an active task + `current_stage` (a Worker, or the Controller self-executing on owner say-so), re-run `bin/yitc-v2 stage <current_stage> --task T-XXXX`** to re-deliver that stage's bundle (the specs + work-verbs). A **session with no active lifecycle stage does a seed-only re-read** — there is no stage bundle to re-deliver (no contradiction). This reuses the existing post-compact re-read discipline; it is NOT a new gate. **PLAN axis (per SPEC-0007 §5b):** a session DWELLING in a plan stage re-delivers ASYMMETRICALLY — the live case is **mid-`decomposition`** (a plan at `status: decomposition`, cutting the plan into task cards over several turns): a `/compact` evicts the cut-rules bundle while the executing-leg read-gate's receipt survives on disk, so do TWO COMPLEMENTARY re-orientation steps yourself — (1) re-orient to your POSITION in the plan (current stage + next gate + the cards cut so far) via **`bin/yitc-v2 plan show <slug>`** (the read-only re-orientation), and (2) re-fetch the decomposition cut-RULES bundle via **`bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0070`** (whose §8 names the full bundle). These are complementary, NOT a replacement (`plan show` = where-am-I; SPEC-0070 = the cutting rules). Do **NOT** re-run `plan stage <NAME>` to re-deliver — it is a one-step FSM advancer (re-running the stage already entered is an illegal edge), UNLIKE the non-mutating task `stage <NAME>`.

**Shared coordination-log re-fold (per SPEC-0086).** The `cross outbox`/`cross inbox` counts are a `session start` ECHO over the kernel-owned shared coordination log, **not** a re-readable seed file — so a `/compact` evicts them and re-reading the seed does NOT restore them, and `session start` is not re-run to restore THIS echo (§Refresh's one sanctioned re-run — the seed-receipt refresh — refreshes only that receipt, never this echo). **Re-surface explicitly by RE-FOLDING the log directly: `bin/yitc-v2 cross outbox` / `cross inbox`** (derived, no stored state; the re-fold returns the FULL non-terminal ledger — a superset of the start-time actionable cut: outbox = `from:me` items a peer fixed awaiting MY close; inbox = `to:me` items still `requested` and not yet task-linked). Full re-fold mechanics: `bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0086`.

**Proactive-debt echo re-fold (per SPEC-0007 §5b / SPEC-0119).** The proactive-debt echo — the 3 DERIVED debt views (not-adopted / open-followups / overdue-rechecks) surfaced report-only at the 2 deterministic seams (session-start + land-tail), suppressed-when-clean — is a `session start` / land-tail ECHO, **not** a re-readable seed file, so a `/compact` evicts the session-start line and re-reading the seed does NOT restore it (`session start` is not re-run to restore THIS echo (§Refresh's one sanctioned re-run — the seed-receipt refresh — refreshes only that receipt, never this echo)). **Re-surface it by RE-FOLDING directly: `bin/yitc-v2 debt`** (derived, no stored state; re-computes the CURRENT debt counts, prints nothing when clean — the exact analog of the `cross outbox`/`cross inbox` re-fold). Full mechanics: `bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0119`.

**Frontend-error echo re-fold (`-C` consumer sessions, per SPEC-0007 §5b / SPEC-0171).** An ADOPTING consumer's `session start` ECHOES what is confirmed-broken in the product frontend — one report-only, suppressed-when-clean line (count + the top-2 cluster LABELS + a pointer), folded READ-ONLY from the source that consumer DECLARES under `extensions.adopts[] spec: SPEC-0170`. It is a `session start` ECHO, **not** a re-readable seed file, so a `/compact` evicts it and re-reading the handbook seed does NOT restore it (`session start` is not re-run to restore THIS echo — §Refresh's one sanctioned re-run refreshes only the seed receipt, never this echo). **Re-surface it by RE-FOLDING directly: `bin/yitc-v2 -C <repo> frontend-errors`, invoked BARE** — the bare form resolves the SAME declared source, so the re-fold verb IS the on-demand view verb (the exact `debt` / `cross outbox` shape). Derived, no stored state, no event; unlike the echo, an explicitly-invoked view STATES its silence rather than printing nothing. A consumer whose declared source does not qualify gets its REASON instead of that silence. Full mechanics: `bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0171` (delivery) / `SPEC-0170` (the fold).

**Kernel-signaling reflex line re-derivation (`-C` consumer sessions, per SPEC-0007 §5b).** A `-C` consumer `session start` ECHOES the kernel-signaling reflex (mark a deviation `relates_to: kernel` + `target: yitc-v2` → at `land` it AUTO-ROUTES to the kernel as a `cross request --kind bugfix --to yitc-v2`, NO owner reminder, idempotent by fingerprint; a kernel FEATURE ask `--kind task` stays owner-gated). It is a `session start` echo, **not** a re-readable seed line — so a `/compact` evicts it and re-reading the handbook seed does NOT restore it. **Re-surface it by re-fetching its authoritative home: `bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0085` / `patterns/error-friction-tracking.md §3`** (the rule lives there; `session start` is not re-run to restore THIS echo (§Refresh's one sanctioned re-run — the seed-receipt refresh — refreshes only that receipt, never this echo)). Engine-self sessions never see this line (the kernel's own `land` short-circuits `relates_to:kernel` to itself).

**MCP session-start reconcile re-delivery (per SPEC-0007 §5b / SPEC-0118).** SPEC-0118's `binding:[seed]` surfaces the MCP session-start reconcile (list connected MCP servers → compare against the declared standing set → disable any extra one-off) as a `session start` ECHO — **not** a re-readable seed file, so a `/compact` evicts it and re-reading the handbook seed does NOT restore it (`session start` is not re-run to restore THIS echo (§Refresh's one sanctioned re-run — the seed-receipt refresh — refreshes only that receipt, never this echo)). **Re-surface it by re-fetching its authoritative home: `bin/yitc-v2 graph query SPEC-0118` → `patterns/working-with-mcp-in-v2.md` §session-start reconcile** (the rule lives there; the CONNECT/USE half of this floor stays delivered via the re-readable `graph/floor-trigger-map.md` MCP-use row). Pointer only — the rule is not restated here (P5).

**Verification:** after compact, before your first SUBSTANTIVE action — any edit/write, or any mutating/governed command (the read-only startup calls a session's own `session start` needs are exempt) — confirm you've re-read your audience's seed VIEW (which carries CHARTER §Principle 1) by voicing BOTH anchors aloud in your response — (1) the **anti-complexity** principle (CHARTER §Principle 1), (2) the **deviation-capture reflex** (full procedure `patterns/error-friction-tracking.md`). One principle is not enough. If you cannot voice both, re-read.

## Language

- **Owner-facing communication** (chat replies, briefs, owner-directed messages / pings) — **Russian**.
- **Code, commits, and identifiers** (source, commit messages, task / decision / spec IDs, event & verb names, YAML field keys) — **English**.

This is V2's OWN rule, no longer inherited from the non-normative global `<host-home>/<vendor-adapter>.md` : AGENTS.md is part of the always-loaded session seed, so a `/clear`'d V2 session that holds **zero** global context still has it. **Distinct concern** from CHARTER §Principle 4b (provider-neutral *methodology text* — no provider brand names in normative docs); see it there, this section does not restate it.

**Register — owner-facing prose (chat replies, briefs, pings) (recurring "explain it more simply" asks, 2026-06).** Default to the PLAIN register the owner otherwise has to request with an "explain it more simply" — do NOT wait to be asked. Concretely:
- Lead with one plain line: "what this is / where we are."
- Short sentences, everyday words. Replace or gloss jargon with a plain phrase or analogy on EVERY use, not just the first (e.g. «`patterns/` = the shelf of general reusable practices»).
- Structure as short bold-headed chunks + bullets, not dense paragraphs.
- End with one plain recommendation or question (recommendation first — §Recommendation Default).
- Target: understandable to a capable reader with zero context on this system.

**Keep technical identifiers EXACT — but always gloss them.** Never rename / translate / paraphrase the token itself: verb & command names (`bin/yitc-v2 land`), ids (`SPEC-XXXX` / `T-XXXX` / `E-XXXX` / `X-XXXX`), event names, field keys, file paths. Pair each with a plain gloss in the surrounding sentence (precise token, plain sentence). "Exact" ≠ "unexplained".

This is a REGISTER rule, distinct from the LANGUAGE rule above (Russian vs English) — it governs how plainly owner-facing prose is phrased, not which language.
